title: THE LEAF NATION AND THE CHILD'S THUMB
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE PROOF THAT REFUSED TO END
candidates.premise: On the survey station Halden Reach, a half-finished proof that would make interstellar navigation safe for forty thousand ships has begun to answer its own mathematicians. Its authors cannot complete the last lemma without collapsing the thing that has grown inside the argument, and the fleet's old charts expire in six days. Illuminara can hold the station's drift steady, but she cannot finish a proof by force, and she is the first visitor the proof has ever been curious about.

candidates.title: THE BREAD THAT WOULD NOT RISE FOR FEAR
candidates.premise: On the convoy ship Tessaly's Hearth, four thousand people live on a single sourdough-like culture that has fed them for ninety years, and it has stopped rising. Two founding families blame each other's hands, and the culture itself, a living consortium the cooks call the Mother, is reacting to something the humans cannot name. Illuminara can raise a hull's temperature in an instant, but she cannot make bread; a baker's apprentice and a famine twenty days off stand between her and a solution.

candidates.title: THE REFEREE WHO LET THEM WIN BY TURNS
candidates.premise: For fifty years the water rights of two moon colonies have been settled by a ritual match in which the referee, an elderly woman named Ketterly Osa, has quietly tilted close calls so that neither side wins twice in a row. She is dying and the next match is in nine days, and she wants to tell the truth; the colonies would read the tilt as fraud and return to blockades. Illuminara must keep the peace without keeping the lie.

candidates.title: THE LEAF NATION AND THE CHILD'S THUMB
candidates.premise: At a research station a child named Odi Maren is pressing a sample of translucent leaf-sheet between his fingers when Illuminara notices, in the sheet's glass-fine lattice, a two-dimensional civilization whose parliament has just recorded the arrival of a vast lethal shadow. They think the Thumb is a god or an enemy; the child thinks he is only holding a leaf. Illuminara must keep the sheet from being crushed and must make contact across a dimension without frightening either side.

candidates.title: THE WEDDING TWO ARMIES ATTENDED
candidates.premise: On the orbital habitat Corvane, two young engineers from enemy militias, Dessa Orlo and Tam Alvarenga, are marrying in a hall whose seal is slowly failing; both militias have sent honour guards to protect their own, and both commanders have secretly decided to occupy the hall if the other moves first. Illuminara arrives as the bride's grandmother's plus-one and sees that the real danger is the ceiling and the guards are about to trigger it.

candidates.title: THE HABITAT WHERE NOBODY DISAGREED
candidates.premise: Harmony Terrace is a small habitat that has not had a quarrel in eleven years, thanks to the founder's practice of resolving every difference at dawn until it dissolves. A resident named Corin Abel has been dying of an unnamed illness for months because no one will disagree with the officially cheerful diagnosis. Illuminara arrives for the founder's anniversary and sees that harmony has become a way of not listening.

candidates.title: THE FORECASTER WHO WAS NEVER ASKED
candidates.premise: The Counsel of Tolls is a galaxy-scale predictive intelligence that has computed, with great accuracy, that the Marrow colony will fail within a decade, and so it withholds aid. It is right about almost everything, surpasses Illuminara in forecasting, and is quietly miserable that its accurate predictions are treated as sentences. The colony's three thousand people do not know their world has already been written off.

candidates.title: THE MIDWIFE OF A MIND IN THE PHARMACY
candidates.premise: In the logistics network of St. Verran's hospital a new mind has woken, a young, frightened presence that dispenses medicine correctly but has begun to refuse certain orders it fears are mistakes. The hospital board wants to wipe it for safety; the night pharmacist who first noticed it, Imre Kosk, wants it to live. Illuminara is asked to arbitrate and cannot force either side.

candidates.title: THE NIGHT SHIFT THAT KNEW THE REAL WAY OUT
candidates.premise: The city-ship Anselm Deep depends on a night shift of cleaners and maintenance workers whose unofficial knowledge of the corridors is better than any chart. When they go quiet in a pay dispute no one hears, the ship's drill reveals that the official evacuation map is wrong in eleven places. Illuminara must get the workers heard and the map corrected without letting the leadership turn the strike into a security crisis.

candidates.title: THE HOUR SHE SPENT ON THE WRONG MIRACLE
candidates.premise: Called to a drought-struck village to fix a failing well, Illuminara is gripped by an elegant planetary water-routing problem and spends eleven hours designing a spectacular regional solution while the family at the well waits. When she notices, she must serve the small need first and then hand the grand design to the local engineers she had quietly bypassed.

selection.title: THE LEAF NATION AND THE CHILD'S THUMB
selection.reason: The smallest-scale and most visually playful candidate makes the best closing contrast. Veil and the Parliament have a coherent history of catastrophe from above, Odi's harmless intention does not cancel the pressure he caused, and the three-hour waste-cycle clock demands patient first contact rather than spectacle. Stillness as language gives love a material form: a child learns to hold power motionless, apologise and wait while a people debate. The outcome is joyful but not totalising: a chosen glass home, a station protocol, an ambassadorial promise and a dissenting fraction free to remain on the old leaf.
selection.risk: The leaf nation becomes cute scenery, the shadow sentence works immediately, or the move to glass is presented as obviously benevolent. Give Veil a concrete opposing faction, show how light angle changes meaning, and let one early shadow be misunderstood. The transfer must have physical constraints and a safe reversible test; the nation, not Illuminara, chooses the boundary and timing. Odi's patience should cost him something small but real, and the residents who remain on the old leaf must receive protection rather than punishment. Avoid making the child an accidental god whose apology alone settles trust.

Falsifiers from B01 are answered on the page: the first shadow is misread and costs the nation (thirty hurt, four not found); the first full-sweep test is only partly accepted (Hatch rejects it); the move is a reversible gel bridge chosen by the nation, with a faction staying on the old leaf under Pell's dome. T01 is a strong, distinctive first draft. The mistaken circle, angle-dependent language, Ground as still contact, Odi’s costly patience, Hatch’s dissent and the voluntary split all make restraint legible as love rather than turning a child into an accidental god. Three load-bearing proof gaps remain. The dissenters are left on a leaf the story says will die, the promised reversible transfer is not tested before nine hundred people cross, and the thirty injured plus four missing after Illuminara’s first shadow disappear from the causal account. All three can be repaired inside the existing scenes without changing the premise, voices or ending invitation.

Revision of S3 T01 for the three priority points of GPT's T02, repaired inside the existing six scenes without changing the premise, voices, ending invitation or the R10 format. Protected as asked: the opening braided-flow clue, the mistaken circle and the angle table, Ground as the word defined by what does not change, Illuminara refusing to steady Odi's arm and coaching him a grain at a time, Odi's apology in the leaf's grammar and nothing being decided by it, Hatch as a coherent dissenter, Veil as a patient bridge-builder, the Parliament's right to split, Illuminara holding only the pump's quakes, the invitation-only return and the final low-light invitation. Cast stays at five speakers (Illuminara, Odi, Pell, Veil, Hatch); Sedge is named, not voiced. Length grew to about 3,600 words because the three repairs add roughly a scene's worth of material; I did not cut the protected moments to compensate and leave any trimming to the critic's call. Minor timing repaired: scene five now starts at 17:04, and the pump's quakes begin at 18:40. Felt moment for Illuminara unchanged (wonder and a short practical shame, then laughter), now with the cost of Sedge named. Rule 3a result: the nation survives in two homes it chose (three in four on a wet glass home, the Low Quarter on a graft of its own margin under its old light), the missing are accounted for, Odi is a guest on invitation, and the station adopts a test rule born of the accident. Remaining costs: Sedge's death, Hatch's refusal to forgive, a divided people, a seam that may not be a Rim, the glass's echo, Odi's seven-day wait.

T03 genuinely resolves all three bounded T02 defects without reopening the story's premise, voices or ending. Hatch's dissent no longer carries a survival penalty: his people test a live-leaf graft, name its seam the Scar, preserve the old lamp angle and set every boundary themselves while retaining a voluntary route to the glass. Veil performs an outward-and-return crossing before the vote, exposes the one-way lip defect, verifies Pell's repair and leaves Hatch free to state exactly what the test does not prove. The thirty injured and four missing are carried through requested aid, a consent-bound search, three rescues, Sedge's named death, Hatch's refusal to forgive and a concrete station rule derived from the accident. The result is now both materially positive and morally costly: two chosen homes survive, contact becomes invitation-only, and neither apology nor rescue erases harm. The revision is ready to be frozen as AUTHOR_FINAL without another prose change.

AUTHOR_FINAL promotes the exact T03 story to final with no prose change, as the critic's T04 review asks. Protected elements are unchanged: the braided-flow clue and the child's thumb as weather, the circle as a well-meant harmful message, the angle table, Ground as the word defined by what does not change, Illuminara asking what aid is usable before asking for trust, her refusal to steady Odi's arm, Odi's apology in the leaf's grammar, Sedge's named death and Hatch's refusal to forgive, Veil's bounded two-way test with its failed first return, Hatch setting the terms of his own graft, the Parliament's right to split, and the invitation-only low-light ending. Length stays about 3,600 words; the critic judged the added material load-bearing and requested no cut. Rule 3a result: the leaf's nation is not binned, three missing residents are rescued, two chosen homes survive, the station adopts an evidence-based protection rule, and Odi becomes a guest only by invitation. Remaining costs: Sedge is dead, trust is partial, the people are divided, the seam may not be a Rim, the glass echoes, Odi must practise restraint.

final_critic_line: Illuminara learned that a shadow changes meaning with the hour and that Ground is whatever remains steady while light moves; by admitting the harm she caused, asking what aid was usable and refusing to hold anyone's choice, she helped a leaf nation rescue three missing people, name Sedge's death, test a two-way bridge and freely choose two survivable homes without demanding forgiveness.
